question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 12 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 1 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{21}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 12 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 1 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 7 & 1 & -4 \\ 5 & -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 7 & 1 & -4 \\ 5 & -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 1 & -4 \\ -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 1 & -4 \\ -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
